To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of intracellular Ca2+ stores by carbachol in individual cells of rat intestinal smooth muscle is all‐or‐none in nature.
carbachol (a cholinergic agonist) induces all‐or‐none responses in the rat intestine, in terms of the release of Ca2+ from internal stores and the generation of Ca2+ currents.

the threshold concentration for the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores is different in different cells of rat intestinal smooth muscle, though the concentration‐dependent release occurs in all cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism underlying the all‐or‐none response of intestinal smooth muscle cells.
the mechanisms of Ca2+ transients in the smooth muscles of rat intestine.
the mechanisms by which smooth muscle cells of the intestine respond to acetylcholine (ACh), which acts on muscarinic receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CCh‐induction of the release of Ca2+ from the internal stores of the rat intestinal cells is a threshold phenomenon.
the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores in the rat intestinal smooth muscles is a stochastic process.
the CCh‐inducible Ca2+ release from the SR takes place in an ‘all‐or‐nothing’ fashion in individual cells, but that the threshold for the Ca2+ release varies among cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the threshold of the release of Ca2+ is determined in each cell and that the release of Ca+2 in each cell is independent of the release of the other cells, even if the cells are coupled by gap junctions.
CCh‐stimulated release of stored Ca is all‐or‐none in single cells of the rat intestine, but the threshold for release varies from cell to cell.
the CCh‐induction of Ca2+ release from the intracellular stores is an all‐or nothing response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CCh‐induce Ca2+‐release is an all‐or nothing phenomenon in single smooth muscle cell of the rat intestinal muscle.
the release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores is an all-or-nothing event in single smooth muscle.
we were able to show the presence of a novel mechanism for calcium signaling in the smooth muscle cells of the intestine.
